## Principal corrections and distinctions

1. The invariant source's reversed-meridian matrix is Q=P_mark S. It is not interchangeable with the required FAMILY matrix. Positive base loops, clockwise analytic root decks, affine twist vectors and collar integration orientations are transported explicitly.
2. The order-four Albanese lattice contains the factor 1/2. Its nome is iw/216; the order-three nome is −w²/48³, and their relation is q1=(27/64)q2². The Engel reference lift is fixed at c=0, so its parameter is w² with that specific linearization.
3. The degree-one cusp-torsion assertion is false in AC26's original PDF, Remark 9.21 on page 81. It is not merely a transcription error. The full local module calculation proves that degree-one torsion is supported on the two multiple fibres, while degree-two cusp torsion remains. Remark 1.3 must be qualified by degree.
4. The historical FAMILY questions C.3.3 and E.1.5 retain their entire local arguments, but their printed headings and inventory kinds identify the subsequent complete boundary and virtual-Euler exclusions. They are not counted among the outstanding questions.
5. The strongest filling obstruction uses the actual affine origins. The former reading's unverified origin-comparison step has been derived from the marked cusp gluing, with the radial gamma defect and all finite twists retained. A linear lattice comparison alone is not treated as that proof.
6. The obsolete global-meridians program failed. Its corrected successor and the independent quotient fixed-space computation passed. Both outputs remain. The all-fan homology program required a dependency-ordered rerun; its initial failure and successful rerun remain.
7. The normalized norm and the Betti measure require the stated orientation and factor 12. The Cayley coordinate is chi=(tau−i)/(tau+i), with k=pi²E4(i) and z=k chi². Source-local symbols and scalings are transported by the shared notation dictionary; the earlier report's k_chi shorthand was ambiguous and is superseded by this explicit formula.
8. The two source entries named Brunella1999 are different works. The forms paper has been given the separate key Brunella1999Forms; the original forms PDF identifies Marco Brunella, overriding an erroneous author field on the publisher HTML. Metadata checking does not by itself verify its use in a proof.
9. The analytic base-change checks retain their precise domains. Reduced-base Bănică–Stănăşilă statements are not silently used for nonreduced Kuranishi bases. The local one-variable Kuranishi algebra and the nonzero actual-family map provide the required argument.
10. The provisional MAPS fourfold torsion differential has a complete Fox/Wang calculation in the audit supplement. The finite Smith computations alone would not identify the geometric differential. The earlier factor-four shortcut is not retained as a proof.
11. The general-cusp deck quotient uses the actual triangle-monodromy deck group. The fundamental group of the punctured base is not substituted for that deck group. Compact chart subsets, rather than a false assertion of properness on an entire open chart, supply the quotient separation argument.
12. The two marked modular collisions 50/II and 56/II now have a complete geometric realization proof, primitive junction and gauge calculations, and an independently rerun exact certificate. Matching numerical invariants alone is not used to identify a geometric filling.

The rank-six adapter distinguishes homology matrices A-transpose and B-transpose from the inverse matrices defining the left cohomology action. Exact finite computations do not replace the geometric argument.

## PUSH: actual cusp origin and non-filling

The following full arguments were read and re-derived in this writing:
B.4.4, B.4.9, B.4.18–19, B.4.24, B.4.27, B.4.30–33. The original
independent reader's checks of B.4.24, B.4.26, B.4.30 and B.4.33 are also
preserved: `reviews/S6_FINAL_INTAKE_20261116/EXPERT_POSITION.md`, Claude Fable
5.2 (Anthropic), effort max, 16 November 2026. The high-effort final intake
explicitly did not read B.4.24 or B.4.26; the expert subsequently did.

* B.4.4: proper direct image of the relative bi-anticanonical line bundle is
  a torsion-free rank-two sheaf on a disc, hence locally free. The pencil is
  meromorphic on the total space. The graph gives the required meromorphic
  map. After vertical components are removed, the critical image is analytic
  and its three individually marked degree-one branches extend. The
  cross-ratio normalizing their target positions is meromorphic. No
  central Kähler hypothesis is used.
* B.4.27: on a sequence of point blowups of a bidisc, the exceptional tree
  gives H²(Z)=Z^N and the other required H¹,H³,H⁴ vanish. Laurent-chart
  computations give H^j(O)=0 for j>0. The exceptional intersection matrix is
  unimodular, so its divisor classes generate Pic. For the two permitted
  logarithmic divisor sheaves, H¹(M^gp)=0 and H²(M^gp)=Z^N. The period map
  on H² is diagonal with nonzero factors 12ma_i and 12ma_i+12nb_i. Its
  injectivity yields H¹(A)=0. The forbidden first-character order along the
  strict r-axis is retained throughout.
* B.4.30: the analytic logarithmic de Rham comparison supplies a locally free
  canonical extension without a Kähler assumption. In a semistable chart
  t=x_1...x_k, k≤3, the closed relative logarithmic one-form sheaf and the
  normalized invariant-form subsheaf are t-saturated inside the canonical
  extension. They agree off t=0 and therefore agree. Reduced connected
  central fibres give torsion-freeness of R¹O via the multiplication-by-t
  sequence. Angular periods are integral in the primitive cocharacter
  lattice; integration term by term divides by nonzero integers of absolute
  value at least one. Characters are units times integral monomials.
  Chains of local charts and sections across the connected fibre extend
  differences. The coefficient-ideal blowup lowers the excess fibre
  dimension by one; normal finite surface multisections are Cohen–Macaulay,
  and finite flat after the stated normalization. Principalization and
  resolution reduce generic exceptional points to t=unit·prod(x_i^m_i).
  A divisible root and a height-one lattice-polygon subdivision give a smooth
  reduced normal-crossings model. Only the analytic toroidal correspondence,
  not a projective semistable-reduction theorem, is used. Generic cyclic
  splitting of finitely many multisections gives a uniform norm exponent.
  Hartogs extends the normalized character units and their inverses across
  the finitely many omitted points. The integral first-character exclusion
  is unchanged by this operation. Literature statements are checked below.
* B.4.31: the finite set of angular meridians is permuted by the base
  monodromy and lies in ker E. On the quotient by delta the remaining
  rank-two representation is the full SL_2(Z), which has no nonzero finite
  orbit. Every angular meridian is therefore a multiple of delta.
* B.4.32: origin changes contribute only delta. The cap-section defect is a
  flat class in Lambda_Q/Q delta. The fixed lines for the two finite
  monodromies are Q(1,2,-4) and Q(1,3,-3), with zero intersection.
* B.4.33: the extending origin has zero gamma defect against both local
  origins; the actual transition has nonzero gamma winding. Its norm gives
  0=D n with D,n>0. This contradicts a filling. The exact constant and sign
  identities were independently recomputed in
  `code/editorial/root_cusp_origin_audit.py`.

The actual-origin issue left outside the scope of the expert's check is
resolved as follows. With gamma=(6mu,C-s-12v), delta=(0,1), the transition is
F=(mu(s+12v)/2,C(s+12v)/12-(s+12v)^2/24+6v). Its s- and v-differences are
the claimed periods, including Delta_v(n)F=n gamma-6n(n-1)delta. In the
ordinary/cusp overlap, the comparison has second constant
D=C_0,21-12kappa_0. The origin sigma(c)=(-c mu/2,-c²/24-cD/12) gives exactly
the closing cocycle. Root's independent polynomial calculation and the maps
auditor's independent reconstruction agree. Integral deck factors
exp(2pi i h lambda_1) are one. No conclusion rests on a formal cocycle whose
geometric origin has not been matched.

## PUSH E.2: stability chain (transferred to Paper II)

All of E.2.4–E.2.24 have now been read, including E.2.7 in this writing.
Their expanded full text is preserved in `push_E2_stability_for_II.tex`.
The mathematical steps below passed; remaining exact source verification is
tracked separately in the bibliography record.

* E.2.5: the relative Picard vector group gives a unique root
  L^D=K^A for A=12kl and D=kl-3k-4l≠0. Direct image injects the two generic
  sections into the central space of sections. The valid CDP theorem on
  nonholomorphic meromorphic maps and c_3 excludes indeterminacy on S^6.
  Two independent functions would produce local indeterminacy, so the
  algebraic dimension is one. Stein factorization gives P¹ and the residual
  effective fixed divisor.
* E.2.6: for positive canonical slope, c_1(K_F)=0 and surface theory imply
  kappa(F)≥0; positive kappa would make a meromorphic ratio nonconstant on a
  general fibre. Thus K_F is torsion and the horizontal fixed divisor is
  absent. Flat irreducible general pencil divisors and connected central
  normalization remove the vertical fixed part and force degree one.
  A smooth surface with the torus topology and these invariants is a complex
  torus. The reduced fraction of 1/m+1/n recovers coprime m,n. Opposite signs
  would make the canonical bundle torsion, contradicting the volume/Stokes
  argument.
* E.2.7: bounded z=exp(-pi i c/(kl)) extends. The three critical sections may
  collide but their normalizing projective transformation is meromorphic.
  A fixed ordinary target gives a smooth compact torus family over the disc,
  with identity H_1 monodromy. A zero of order d in z contributes S_-h,
  h=2kld>0. The base path has ordinary, finite peripheral, or cusp peripheral
  monodromy. Finite cases cannot cancel S_-h after taking order 3 or 4.
  In the cusp case I+nN-hE is identity only if n=h=0, since its u-to-w
  coefficient is n. The maximum principle excludes the outer radius.
  Translation comparisons do not affect H_1.
* E.2.8: Alexander-duality ranks force irreducible fibres and trivial
  rank-one H¹ monodromy. A horizontal effective divisor would give a
  topologically trivial effective divisor on a class-C normalization, which
  is impossible by a Kähler integral. The negative-slope residual case has
  a class-VII normalization with b_1=1.
* E.2.9: H⁰(V(-nD)) stabilizes to zero by finite dimensionality, Krull
  intersection and analytic continuation; the full nonreduced support is
  handled by its finite filtration. Relative Gorenstein fibre duality gives
  the complementary H² vanishing for large n. Compactness supplies a common
  n; positive base twist kills H²,H³, while a separate negative twist kills
  H⁰. Along an affine holomorphic Picard line each jumping set is proper
  analytic, so one bundle avoids all three. Hence chi(B)≤0. For B=T_X,
  Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch gives chi=c_3/2=1, a contradiction. This proof
  allows a non-Kähler general fibre and is not a duplicate of CDP E1.
* E.2.10: the previous horizontal-vanishing result reduces either slope to
  the vertical argument of E.2.6.
* E.2.11: under the explicitly assumed good Jacobian extension on a bidisc,
  Hartogs extends the torsor fields. Completeness on compact fibres gives
  a torus action. A connected stabilizer acts trivially on the fibre tangent
  by holomorphic representation theory and on the base quotient; averaging
  splits the tangent representation, then local linearization forces the
  stabilizer to be trivial. Finite isotropy remains. A flowbox gives a finite
  transverse map C²→B; an isolated critical point would force a critical
  determinant curve. Thus the map is a submersion and the finite isotropy
  is trivial as well.
* E.2.12–13: finite monodromy forces its order to divide the local exponent,
  so the finite period model extends after its holomorphic root. A cusp
  unipotent power cannot be identity. On a punctured bidisc the period
  kernel extends, supplying the good Jacobian required in E.2.11.
  Normalizing r^m=a^m·unit gives free unramified root charts; purity then
  forces the exact central multiplicity. No unproved extension of an
  arbitrary Jacobian is assumed.
* E.2.14: comparison with a central regular bidisc extends the coefficient
  of the normalized delta field; a zero would divide the generator by the
  base parameter and contradict its primitive choice. The complete
  period-one action is transported equivariantly. A collapse of the finite
  marked tori would extend the delta flow to a compact elliptic action with
  a fixed point, impossible for a nontrivial compact complex group action.
* E.2.15: in the remaining isotrivial case the marked periods are constant.
  A pluricanonical volume integral gives
  integral |q^(-D-2A)phi(1/q)|^(2/A)<infinity. Subharmonic estimates imply
  pole order at most A-1. If D≥-A this would make the entire nonvanishing
  phi extend with a zero at infinity. Here D/A≥-1/2, so collapse is excluded.
* E.2.16: the finite multiplicities are exact and the critical supports
  irreducible. The fundamental group maps onto the triangle group
  Delta(m,n,d); for d≥2 it is nontrivial (including the (3,4,2) finite
  case), hence d=1. Euler number and the invariant-cycle statement then
  determine the cusp normalization's first Betti number.
* E.2.17: conservation of the plane Milnor number and nonsplitting give a
  single ordinary node in transverse flowboxes. At the fixed curve the
  invariant function has the form T g(T,z), T=xy, and g(0,z) is a nonzero
  section of O(2). A double zero would split a plane singularity into two
  critical points with the same critical value, forbidden by nonsplitting.
  Thus there are precisely two simple zeros and the actual family has the
  claimed xy/xyz models. Normalizations vary smoothly.
* E.2.18: the normalization has b_1=0,b_2=4 and a hexagon of six (-1)
  curves. Contracting three alternate curves leaves b_2=1 and a triangle
  of (+1) curves. Its canonical degree is negative, giving P²; the original
  pair is its blowup at the three vertices. The toric logarithmic tangent
  frame persists by base change.
* E.2.19: conductor transition matrices of logarithmic vector fields are
  constant on each compact component and identity off the central
  parameter, hence identity everywhere. The normal-crossings equalizer has
  no extra triple-point condition. Complete commuting fields and primitive
  period loops recover the actual two-dimensional torus action, including
  its full central lattice and the integral toric characters.
* E.2.20: a stratified q-preserving transport identifies the actual cusp
  covering. The union of maximal infinite-fan charts is simply connected;
  the deck group is Lambda/Lambda_tor. Crossing q=ab expresses adjacent
  origin ratios as powers of q times units, with no essential singularity.
  Unimodular triple characters identify the actual charts by Laurent
  monomials times these units. A finite fundamental domain gives a common
  neighbourhood; no infimum over infinitely many shrinking radii is used.
* E.2.21: finite affine classes are integral and locally constant. Vector
  remainders are removed by finite averaging. Collar period classes,
  including the cusp, are constant. The exact sequence with O·delta and
  O(-infinity) has H¹=0, and a Cauchy/Laurent solution depends holomorphically
  on parameters. This identifies the actual whole family.
* E.2.22: propagation removes finitely many analytic discrete layers for
  the pencil, critical sections, roots, normalization and NC rank tests,
  toric action, and period kernel. Identities propagate from the known open
  set; the real determinant stays in the admissible component, including
  at finite roots. Fill the layers in reverse order using E.2.21. A deleted
  layer may accumulate only at an earlier deleted one, which this ordering
  handles.
* E.2.23: the known locus is locally open; connected Riemann-surface
  propagation makes it closed. Finite projection of an arbitrary analytic
  branch to a polydisc and a complex line yields a curve connecting a
  known point to the tested point. Normalize that curve and apply the disc
  result. The recovered multiplicities distinguish the components.
* E.2.24: the C-infinity Kuranishi local product/retraction transports the
  analytic-base result to the space of integrable structures. Each specified
  pair gives an open and closed invariant set and therefore an open and
  closed subset in the diffeomorphism quotient. The cited precise local

  assertion about moduli spaces.

## External analytic sources already opened and matched

* Illusie–Kato–Nakayama (2005), Theorems 6.2–6.4: proper separated fs log
  smooth analytic morphism, log-smooth base (or exactness), constant
  unipotent coefficients, and torsion-free characteristic cokernels in the
  semistable charts give the ordinary locally free canonical log de Rham
  extension used above. No polarization or Kähler condition is added. The
  2007 erratum addresses the algebraic Hodge statement 7.1, not 6.3.
* Kajiwara–Kato–Nakayama (2008), Definitions 1.2.3–1.2.6, Lemma 1.2.9,
  §§1.3 and 5.1.1–5.1.2, Theorem 5.3.2: the pairing and admissible ghost
  data define an unpolarized log complex torus. Pullback preserves the
  required admissibility/nondegeneracy. A Y-invariant fan with full support
  and finitely many Y-orbits gives a proper log-smooth analytic model.
  Projectivity is not asserted or needed. The diagonal ghost data in the
  application satisfy the face-by-face nondegeneracy conditions.
* Bierstone–Milman (1995 preprint), Theorems 1.6 and 1.10: analytic
  embedded resolution and principalization on relatively compact sets;
  these, rather than a compactification theorem, are used locally.
* Parusiński (1990), Corollary 1.2 and its coefficient-ideal proof, pp.3–5
  of the manuscript: finite projections and principalized coefficients
  lower the excess fibre dimension. The proof has been read and matched
  to the proper local excess-one application.
* Enokizono–Hashizume (2024), Lemma 2.14 and proof: analytic strict toroidal
  subdivisions correspond to proper modifications. Only this local
  correspondence is used; the projective hypotheses of the main theorem
  are not imported into the analytic non-filling proof.

# Technical corrections and distinctions to preserve

Checker: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode, effort Pro), effort Pro, writing run, 17 November 2026 UTC. This note records specific findings, not a blanket verification of the CDP return. Exact per-result scopes and remaining dependencies are in `result_audit.json`; exact opened source locators and fingerprints are in `references_verified.json`.

## A.2.6: the normalized differential module

The sentence identifying the raw differential image is false as written. Its exact replacement is:

> The B-module generated by the differential image, where B=C{t}, is t^4 B dt.

For R=C{t^5,t^6,t^7}, the actual R-module image is R⟨t^4,t^5,t^6⟩dt. Its valuation set omits 7 and 8, so it is not t^4B dt. After extension to B and quotient by torsion, the generated module is t^4B dt. The following determinant computation is normalized and therefore still gives 19−4=15. The primeness, critical-locus, transverse-cusp and symbolic-square counterexample proofs all survive this correction. The exact polynomial/semigroup program has been rerun successfully. The full corrected statement and proof are retained in `corrected_A1_1_A2_6_full_proofs.tex`.

## A.1.1: replace the undefined lead reference

Replace “the two vanishings in Lead 1” by the two explicit assumptions H^0(S,N^*⊗A)=0 and H^0(S,Q⊗A)=0. They are precisely the hypotheses needed in the two long exact sequences to identify H^0(S,V⊗A) with ker δ_A. The corrected full block preserves labels A:filtration1 and A:filtration2. Its pre-statement definitions of N^*, V, T, Q and A must accompany it.

## D.1.14: placement and duplicate-method credit

The SL₂(ℤ) group calculation belongs with Paper I's monodromy. Its kernel method agrees with FAM F1.1; it is not a mathematically independent method and should not be identified with FAM F1.2. The full proof is in `paperI_CDP_D1_14_group_proof.tex`. Preserve the exact source concordance while using one coherent exposition.

Its record must retain the historical open status and add the later resolution. ## Fujimoto1988: exact false statement and retained earlier credit

The original definition on pp.91–92 permits proper holomorphic elliptic fibre spaces with smooth source and base and connected fibres; it does not assume a Kähler source or projectivity. Theorem 2.8 and Corollary 2.10, pp.96–97, were opened together with the full proof. For m>1 and 0<|q|<1, the smooth compact Hopf threefold

H_m=(ℂ³\{0})/⟨(a,b,c)↦(qa,q^m b,q^m c)⟩

maps to ℙ² by [a:b:c]↦[a^m:b:c]. It has connected generic elliptic fibre ℂ*/q^ℤ and a multiplicity-m fibre over the line {a^m=0}, whose self-intersection is one. The complement of that line is ℂ². Thus both the asserted cyclic quotient of the complement's fundamental group and the divisibility m|C² fail. The source's normalization of ξ^m=s_D^m splits into m graphs; its asserted connected degree-m Stein cover does not follow. This is an exact counterexample to the printed theorem and corollary, not a judgment about the rest of the paper.

Fujimoto's Example 3.4(1), p.99, already contains a Kodaira-dimension-one component in an abelian-surface degeneration. That prior construction credit must remain even when explaining the defect in Theorem 2.8. The original pages were opened through web retrieval; a failed direct download is not described as a retained PDF.

## Analytic source hypotheses

Grauert1960 §6 Hauptsatz IIa, p.59, was read in the original scan, including its complete proof. It is the proper analytic formal-functions theorem for a coherent sheaf and does not require projectivity or reducedness. It therefore supplies the exact formal-functions input used in PUSH B4.11. The 1963 correction retracts a closedness assertion about the §7 base-change failure locus; it does not invalidate IIa. For cohomology jumping loci and constant-zero top-cohomology base change, use the independently opened Bănică–Stănăşilă finite-complex and cohomological-flatness results, with the reduced-base hypothesis stated when the converse requires it.

Kulikov's 1981 §7 explicitly says that the relevant selector uses only ruled current maximal components. Its §8 removes the earlier distinguished-component and H^1(dual complex)=0 steps. The 1977 local contraction, sigma-atlas, fibre cleanup and reverse-order overlap restoration were checked in the original, then matched to these 1981 alterations. Consequently UN77/81/84 may use the local algorithm under their displayed hypotheses without claiming that the entire 1977 projective theorem holds in that setting. Diagnostic resolution components must not be counted as retained global modification stages.

Nakano1970 alone is not the final sufficient blowdown theorem: its stated extra condition is removed, and its cohomological proof repaired, by Fujiki–Nakano1971. The actual ordinary blowdown input in UN64 is the corrected theorem with a holomorphic projective-space-bundle exceptional divisor and normal O(−1) on its fibres.

Gross–Siebert2006I classifies the relevant central algebraic log spaces. UN71 must retain its explicit analytic-to-algebraic conductor comparison and its independent construction of an actual proper smoothing; a classification of central log spaces is not a uniqueness theorem for analytic smoothing germs.

## Distinct no-horizontal-divisor results

CDP E1 assumes H²(Y,ℝ)=0 and a Kähler general fibre for an arbitrary compact total space. PUSH E2.9 assumes a complex structure on S⁶ and irreducibility of every reduced fibre, and can have non-Kähler fibres. Its argument uses opposite Picard twists and χ(T)=1. They are not duplicate statements. Both proofs and both hypothesis sets should remain available in Paper II, with cross-references where the arguments overlap.

## C4g: integral torsion in the original affine family

The statement is valid, but its proof incorrectly asserts H²(Y,ℤ)=0 for every admissible original affine twist. For d=|p|>1, E19 gives H₁(Y,ℤ)=H₂(Y,ℤ)=ℤ/dℤ, and the universal coefficient theorem therefore gives H²(Y,ℤ)=ℤ/dℤ. Every ambient first Chern class is torsion, so its pullback to the free group H²(dP₆,ℤ) is still zero. Since H¹(dP₆,O)=0, the pulled-back line is trivial, exactly as needed.

The subsequent invocation of C4f also requires repair: that theorem assumes integral CDP hypotheses, which these members do not satisfy. All three named families satisfy b₁=b₂=b₃=0 and possess a nonzero effective Cartier fibre. The already proved C.1.3 consequently gives h²(Y,T_Y⊗L)≥1 for every twist, including every torsion Picard component. This proves the conclusion without extending C4f beyond its hypotheses. The full corrected statement and proof are saved as `corrected_C4g_full_proof.tex`.

## E14 and E16: formula typography

In E16, formula (E.16.3) has a literal tab followed by `ext{is represented by}`; restore `\text{is represented by}`. In E14, the raw subscripts `P'_epsilon` and `f_epsilon` should use the TeX command `\epsilon`. These are typesetting corrections; the associated formulas and full proofs have been checked separately.

## Verification boundaries

The finite programs check their displayed identities, lattice matrices, transition formulas or bounded graph cases. They do not certify all analytic arguments. The parent-alignment graph program uses a fixed random seed and is not exhaustive. Each execution manifest records the exact copied program, original path, hash, exit status and output. A per-row “proof followed” record still lists any unexamined classification source or upstream proof. Full extracted blocks occasionally include the next statement's preparatory text, and pre-statement definitions must be recovered from the canonical source when drafting.

## E6: exact Douady locator and a relative source family

Douady1966's graph theorem is Section10.2, Theorem1, printed p.87; its Section10 is headed Application, not Appendix. The theorem as stated has a fixed compact source. The complete corrected E6 proof constructs the needed relative graph germ from the absolute Douady space of the actual total space times P¹: the unit and a finite cohomology complex give π_*O_R=O_H on the full nonreduced germ; coordinate functions then give H→S; Section10.1 Proposition1 gives the open isomorphism locus. This retains the original all-Artin-order argument and does not apply Horikawa's stronger H²-injectivity theorem without its hypothesis. The full block is corrected_E6_full_proof.tex.

## C2c: the complex-disc realization of Mumford's polyhedral model

Mumford1972 Section6 is formulated over a complete discrete valuation ring, not directly over a complex analytic disc. The corrected proof supplies the actual analytic comparison: the unimodular triangular fan has smooth charts t=x₁x₂x₃; lattice shears act by (z₁,z₂)↦(t^{ℓ₁}z₁,t^{ℓ₂}z₂); normalized logarithms provide a compact fundamental-domain argument and proper discontinuity; the quotient generic fibre is a product of elliptic curves. Thus every even Euler number is realized by a proper analytic degeneration with smooth total space. The original polyhedral/stratum/polarization result remains credited at its exact formal scope. The full block is corrected_C2c_full_proof.tex.

## New source openings and computations

The publisher full text of Csaba Nagy's *Extended surgery theory for simply-connected 4k-manifolds*, Compositio Mathematica 162 (2026), was retrieved. Theorem 1.4 exactly supplies the inertia criterion used in F.4.1: for a closed 3-connected eight-manifold inertia is trivial precisely when p1 is divisible by eight. Since Theta8 is Z/2, otherwise the inertia group is all of Theta8. The record's claim that this reference could not be opened is superseded for this writing. The application remains dependent on the manifold's verified connectivity and Pontryagin class. The HTML source and extraction are in `sources/external/maps_audit/`, outside the deliverables; provenance and SHA-256 are in `external_provenance.json`.

Huize Jin's arXiv:2608.26698v2 PDF was retrieved from arXiv. Proposition 3.1 gives the bordism invariant (-p1*x+4*x^3)/24. Lemma 4.8 and Theorem 4.9 give cube values 1,8 on the primitive and double-sphere Dehn twists, and the rank-two integral Torelli classification of S2 x S3. These are the actual source statements required by MAPS B.6.18. A full geometric match of the actual return to those invariants is still in progress.

Alarcón and Forstnerič's *Oka-1 manifolds* (2025), Definitions 2.1, 7.7, 7.11, the observation preceding Proposition 7.13, and Proposition 7.13(d), were opened and matched to MAPS F.3.8–F.3.9. The proof correctly uses an LSAP fibre-bundle section theorem, not the unanswered assertion that every Oka-1 fibre bundle is Oka-1. The explicit spanning tube is valid: its nine real integer directions are a complex basis; all lines lie uniformly inside det(Im Z)>0; least singular value is at least 1/sqrt(3), and radius 1/4 suffices. The supplied exact verifier was rerun and passed. F.3.11 imposes bounded correction at one retained cusp while other finite points remain punctures; it must not be strengthened to simultaneous good reduction at every puncture.

`fourfolds_nonselfdual.py`, `fourfolds_oka_tubes.py`, and `fourfolds_periods.py` were copied unchanged to `code/maps_audit/` and rerun under the supplied primary Python runtime. Outputs are saved beside them. The exact matrix, Smith, finite covering-index, genus-two discriminant, exterior-square quotient, and all four nonzero Z/2 torsion-residue assertions pass. The output itself states that H2=H3=0 requires the geometric identification of d2; a successful arithmetic run is not treated as a substitute for that identification.

## Proof readings performed so far

MAPS A.1.1–A.2.2 and B.1.1–B.3.3 have been read step by step. The algebraic and homotopy arguments are internally consistent. External source matches for stable homotopy and APS remain to be completed. B.1.1's use of doubling the stable comparison removes its mod-two pi1 obstruction, and the remaining H3 class restricts trivially because the monodromy-invariant vector d lies in ker(gamma). This is sufficient to identify the framed regular inverse image with the Lie-framed T3. The matrix/finite coset computations remain to be rerun; the topological argument recognizes negative-imaginary-w fixed loci by a semifree circle action and positive-imaginary-w fixed loci by determinant-one solid-torus meridians. They do not classify the embedding S3 into S6.

MAPS F.2.5–F.2.6, F.3.5–F.3.11 and F.4.1 have been read in full. The explicit F.3.5–F.3.7 construction uses the primitive exterior square of a genus-two variation and a nonsplit trivial-line extension, not a polarized three-torus family. The H1(P*) vanishing follows from root-line coarse degrees 0,-1,-1. # Independent reading of the remaining MAPS F proofs

Reader: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode, effort Pro), 17 November 2026, separate root writing/checking agent. No human review is asserted. These events preserve the earlier partial readings; they do not overwrite them. Complete receiving-proof reading, imported dependency closure, source comparison and computation rerun are recorded separately.

## Complete receiving proofs read and re-derived in the first batch

- **F.2.2:** The totient bound follows termwise from the prime-power product, whose only factor below one is 1/2 at 2 to the first power. Thus n ≤ 50 is a proved exhaustive cutoff. The characteristic-polynomial multiplicities and the even real 1/−1 eigenspace test establish only necessary spectral types. The actual enumeration is being rerun and its output will be checked separately.
- **F.2.3:** Blowing up a smooth interior point of the cusp changes the three even middle homology groups by one free generator, by the ball/disc-bundle Mayer–Vietoris calculation, while retaining every peripheral datum. The stronger fixed-Kuhn-model question is expressly excluded from this counterexample.
- **F.2.7:** Killing all fibre loops in van Kampen leaves the cyclic root-deck relation at each finite point and kills the cusp meridian. The two-point quotient is cyclic of gcd order. The reflected spherical/Euclidean/hyperbolic triangles give an explicit nontrivial representation for every three-point multiplicity list ≥ 2. No total-space classification is assumed.
- **F.2.15:** Coprime affine multiplicities force one odd linear order, and the cusp product forces both determinants positive. Semisimplicity, conjugate-pair decomposition and even multiplicities of both real eigenvalues give a commuting complex structure at each finite generator. This makes no simultaneous-period assertion.
- **F.2.8:** Multiplying (AB−I)^2 = 0 by A on the left and B inverse on the right gives BA+AB inverse = 2I. For B-fixed v, invertibility of B+I gives Av=v. Its at least two-dimensional fixed space contradicts the required one-dimensional global invariant space. The remaining coprime-order list is a finite filter only.
- **F.2.9:** The global invariant vector/covector pairing vanishes because ker N = im N. Averaging at either finite generator makes restriction of global covectors injective, hence a+b ≤ f_i. Parity then forces b=0 and both f_i=2. A fixed line of the quotient would make a two-dimensional trivial finite-order module upstairs; its dual analogue is excluded likewise. A degree-four irreducible cyclotomic summand permits only submodule dimensions one or four, both excluded. All arguments are rational, not integral classification.
- **F.2.10:** The Hom-sheaf Euler number 2 forces a rational nondegenerate symmetric form. The primitive exterior-square lift makes the cusp a rank-one symplectic transvection; the displayed spectra are disjoint, and the difference has rank one. The common-invariant-subspace argument proves both matrices cyclic, contradicting the repeated eigenvalue of the finite semisimple lift. The same reasoning applies to the stated fourth/sixth repetitions. An explicit elementary proof of the classical Sp4-to-SO5 bridge will be inserted, so this step will not remain an unexplained isomorphism name.
- **F.2.11:** Finite-split extension rows have dimension eight modulo the injective five-dimensional coboundary image. Vanishing parabolic cohomology makes cusp restriction an isomorphism onto a three-dimensional space. Square-zero extensions form ann(im N)/row N, dimension one; its zero class has cusp rank two and every nonzero class rank three. Scaling the invariant line gives the stated rational uniqueness.
- **F.2.12:** The modulo-three irreducibility, primitive global extension and primitive cusp give the unbounded Z3-lattice uniqueness argument by reduction and Smith/Nakayama, not a bounded search. The abelian van Kampen quotient forces both coprimality conditions even with arbitrary cusp clutching. Connected mapping-torus fibres and the Wang sequence justify the complete period test. The second finite period row then gives R/m2R, and the complete degree-three Leray/UCT argument puts it in Tor3 H2. Every cited exact matrix/rank/period certificate is a separate pending output check.
- **F.2.13:** The two specified companion constructions use the same unbounded three-adic uniqueness argument. Case B's suspension numerator gives R/3^rR. Case A's integral middle pairing satisfies I²·6² = m2^4 up to a 3-adic unit, hence valuation 2r−1. The free parabolic contribution and the sole free degree-four cusp kernel cannot remove this torsion; UCT places it in H3. Exact Smith/rank/pairing certificates remain separately scoped.
- **F.2.14:** No nontrivial rational one-dimensional character survives the coprime finite orders and unipotent product. Two invariant decomposable rank-two alternating forms would have stable supporting planes intersecting in a forbidden line; thus the alternating-form space has dimension at most one. Cusp degree-two specialization is surjective with zero kernel by the fully stated E.1.3, so global exterior invariants survive Leray and must vanish. The Euler inequality and odd local exterior ranks force both local ranks three, giving the stated eight spectral cases. This remains a necessary filter.
- **F.3.1:** The local degree-one invariant-sheaf comparison and the base-sphere Leray sequence force a=1 and parabolic H1=0 under b1=b2=0. Self-duality makes the degree-two sheaf rank also one. The cusp contributes odd rank three and every holomorphic finite fixed space even rank, so the sheaf Euler characteristic is odd and parabolic H1 cannot vanish. The relevant duality follows from 0→j!V→j*V→point stalks→0 and compactly supported oriented surface duality.
- **F.3.2:** Without self-duality the same argument gives b = sum r_i + 2 − 6(k−1), with each r_i in {2,4,6} and 0≤b≤min(3,r_i). Direct enumeration gives exactly the displayed two- and three-point lists. No existence conclusion is inferred.

## Convention that must remain explicit in Paper III

The rational F constructions use homology generators A transpose and B transpose; their actual cohomology monodromies are A inverse and B inverse, as stated explicitly in the complete F.2.5 proof. Invariant, coinvariant, fixed-space and exterior-rank calculations are unchanged on inverting a finite generator, but this is not a license to change a marked affine or ordered peripheral relation. The common notation adapter must preserve this distinction and the source's ordered matrices.

## Completion of the root receiving-proof assignment

Reader: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode, effort Pro), 17 November 2026. Complete source text was opened in full for every entry below. These are independent receiving-proof derivations, with the separately identified imported inputs retained as dependencies.

- **F.2.24:** The determinant of the abelian peripheral presentation is m1 m2 kappa+m2 r1+m1 r2. The degree-two suspension covering cokernel injects into the terminal Leray term (1,2), so its vanishing forces the minimal multiplicities five and four. The norm onto the primitive vertical fixed line follows from the maximal fixed-vector/covector pairing. The explicit weighted finite sum gives the cap translation, including its sign. Relative cellular duality on the pair of pants identifies the full translation obstruction with the coinvariants: an oriented relative two-cell has coefficient boundaries generated by the monodromy differences. The primitive covector detects that group in this case. The determinant congruences remove the remaining horizontal twists; fibre inversion extends over the symmetric Kuhn fan and preserves the real six-dimensional fibre orientation.
- **F.2.25:** In the integral splitting by a fixed covector-one vector, the primitive rank-one averaging operator is (n/h) lambda phi and f(D)=(f(1)/h) lambda phi. Thus h divides both n and f(1). The mapping-torus suspension period has full cokernel Z/(m/h), including all free cycles. Global exterior-square invariants vanish, so this cyclic group injects into the terminal (1,2) Leray term. UCT therefore forces m=h=n. Evaluating all eight cyclotomic factors gives precisely the two remaining spectral rows; the excluded orders are eliminated for every relative position and lattice, not by a finite sampling assumption.
- **F.2.26:** The coefficient matrix for the ten normal-form equations is unchanged. Its two modified traces determine the displayed remaining cubic factor after the two-dimensional minus eigenspace is split off. The two first-column adjugate identities give the exact irreducibility conic. Substitution on that conic factors D as the stated positive quadratic times positive quartic; independently expanded the sum-of-squares identity. Thus the exceptional consistency locus remains the two points, with the rank-deficient point impossible and the displayed affine-line solution complete. The scalar stabilizer prevents additional conjugacies.
- **F.2.27:** Over Z3, the integral idempotents (1±D³)/2 split the degree-three regular summand from minus identity. The nonzero norm modulo three gives one full Jordan block and hence a cyclic integral basis. Independently computed the four invariant exterior-three basis words and their skew pairing blocks of sizes one and three. Covering and unimodular downstairs duality force a nonzero order-three covering cokernel. The odd irreducible quotient kills the rational global exterior invariants and the relevant coinvariant rank. The terminal (1,3) term injects into a finite extension inside H4, so its torsion cannot disappear into a free filtration kernel. UCT gives the claimed nonzero three-primary H3 torsion.
- **F.2.28:** Killing the fibre image leaves the trivial coprime two-cone quotient, so the full group is abelian without an extra cusp-closure assumption. The relation matrix is block triangular over the torsion coinvariants and the three free peripheral generators, yielding the exact product of orders and the simple-connectivity criterion. When the determinant is a unit, elimination leaves exactly the original torsion group. The complete relative translation obstruction is the integral coinvariant group, not merely its free quotient. The maximal local norm and the same cap translations as F.2.24 remove every vertical twist; the explicit determinant congruences remove all remaining twists and cusp clutching.
- **F.2.29:** The regular five-cycle over Z5 follows from the nonzero fourth nilpotent power. The four-cycle over Z2 is primitive; its rank-one quotient splits because the kernel of the alternating norm equals the integral image of D+1. Integral approximation of an invertible local intertwiner gives a prime-to-p isogeny preserving the normalized translation, so the monomial cap calculation applies to every eligible lattice. Poincare–Lefschetz duality makes the primitive free cusp kernel map onto the unique order-two boundary torsion. The complete Leray filtrations in degrees three and five contain exactly the six displayed tests; finite filtered groups vanish precisely when all their graded pieces vanish. The parabolic kernel uses actual integral peripheral images, without saturation. The explicit inverse-transpose convention and reversal/conjugation of the cusp are retained.

    "text": "## 8. Sources, proof scope and verification\n\nThe original-author TeX of Daniel C. Isaksen, Guozhen Wang and Zhouli Xu, [Stable homotopy groups of spheres, arXiv:2001.04247v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.04247v1), supplies the classical dual coproduct in its section on the Adams spectral sequence, original `ms.tex` lines 483\u2013583. Its low-dimensional table was read as a routing aid. The proof of (1.8) here is the explicit calculation in Sections 2\u20135, including the full correcting cochains; it is not inferred from that table.\n\nDaniel C. Isaksen, [Stable stems, arXiv:1407.8418v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.8418v2), supplies the comparison with the May notation. The precise passages read for this comparison are original `stable-stems-May.tex` lines 904\u20131000 and `stable-stems-tables.tex` lines 50\u2013118, together with the previously recorded introductory coverage. Equations (4.11), (4.6) and (4.10) give the exact classical comparison. The original source archives and per-file hashes are retained in the private reading ledger. No whole-monograph reading or PDF reading is claimed.\n\nThe displayed odd-prime Hopf algebra is defined in (6.1); its coassociativity, cobar signs and degree-six vanishing are proved directly in Section 6. The [actual odd-prime companion](the-original-odd-prime-cooperations-and-degree-six-adams-calculation.md#odd-actual-adams) constructs the actual original cooperations in the needed degrees and proves their degree-six cobar vanishing and receiving Adams comparison directly. No classification of all odd-prime operations is needed for that proof or assumed by the algebraic vanishing theorem.\n\nThe reproducible calculation script expands the complete coproduct, checks both displayed correcting cochains and their full expansions, and computes selected finite cobar kernels and images. Those finite computations are supplementary checks. The argument over \\(\\mathbb F _2[x]\\) in Section 3 and the signed word reduction in Section 6 are what prove the assertions for every length. Neither a finite rank computation nor this algebraic theorem by itself establishes the stable homotopy or framed-bordism conclusion needed by lesson 7.\n\nThe [original coefficient-ring companion](coefficient-rings-and-the-original-degree-six-class.md#coefficient-all-length-receiving) retains the full source polynomial coefficient algebra before inversion, proves both inverse coefficient and grading maps, and applies Theorem 1.1 here to every length. Its complete original matrices then prove that the bidegree \\((2,8)\\) module has exactly the specified polynomial generator and no coefficient torsion. The coefficient multiple receiving \\([\\zeta_1^4|\\zeta_1^4]\\) is displayed with all four original powers. The included topological comparison, geometric framing calculation and [sphere-twist and smooth-recognition proof](sphere-twists-and-the-original-smooth-six-sphere-comparison.md#twist-original-smooth-map) supply the subsequent receiving arguments.\n\nThe [Adams-tower companion](the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits.md#adams-degree-five-cobar), Section 5, extends the complete original module calculation to prove \\(H^{s,s+5}(C^\\bullet(H_{\\mathrm{cl}}))=0\\) for every nonnegative length. Its full difference-four kernel and image, followed by both terms of the existing seven-term correcting-cochain differential, prove the result. Sections 8\u201311 construct the actual coefficient spectrum and establish finite-stage tower convergence. The [arithmetic companion](the-original-adams-tower-and-arithmetic-completion.md#arithmetic-homotopy-groups) now proves the unit-preserving comparison of that limit with the original Moore tower and retains both derived homotopy-group terms. The [actual degree-eight companion](the-actual-mod-two-cooperation-comparison-through-degree-eight.md#actual-eight-bijectivity) identifies the actual mod-two cooperations in the required degrees. The [original geometric framing proof](the-original-six-dimensional-framing-invariant.md#framed-six-original-nullbordism) constructs the full quadratic invariant, proves framed bordism invariance and gives value zero for the original framed homotopy six-sphere, with an actual framed nullbordism. The [sphere-twist and smooth-recognition proof](sphere-twists-and-the-original-smooth-six-sphere-comparison.md#twist-original-smooth-map) now constructs the new interior gluing with its full frame defect, cancels every actual handle and gives the orientation-preserving diffeomorphism to the original six-sphere, homotopic to its original degree-one map.\n\nThis is an author-written teaching proof of classical algebra. No novelty or independent-review claim is made.\n\n\nThe [actual mod-two cooperation companion](the-actual-mod-two-adams-resolution-and-cooperation-maps.md#cooperation-chain-comparison) now constructs both cross-product coordinate maps, the actual cofree Adams resolution and both chain maps and inverse homotopies comparing it with the actual cooperation cobar complex. Its [original diagonal and degree-range proof](the-actual-mod-two-adams-resolution-and-cooperation-maps.md#cooperation-original-diagonal) identifies the generator tied to the original integer two, proves every degree-two reduced coproduct zero, and shows that the degree-six calculation at every word length uses cooperation degrees through eight. The [actual degree-eight companion](the-actual-mod-two-cooperation-comparison-through-degree-eight.md#actual-eight-bijectivity) supplies the required polynomial comparison through degree eight; the [original geometric framing proof](the-original-six-dimensional-framing-invariant.md#framed-six-original-nullbordism) now supplies that value and its actual framed nullbordism.\n\n\nThe [full characteristic-two coordinate proof](the-exact-characteristic-two-coordinate-calculation.md#formal-two-linearization) now supplies the all-ring formal-series calculation and both inverses. The [actual projective-coordinate proof](the-original-projective-coordinate-and-actual-cooperations.md#projective-actual-coproduct) constructs the polynomial-to-cooperation morphism, proves its full coproduct and antipode comparison, and identifies its [first generator with the original integer two](the-original-projective-coordinate-and-actual-cooperations.md#projective-original-two). The [framed slides and index-one removal](framed-handle-slides-and-index-one-removal.md#slide-index-one-cancellation) are now proved in their receiving companion. The [integral handle-chain companion](integral-handle-chains-and-signed-incidences.md#handle-six-seven) now proves the original filtration-to-homology map, every incidence sign, the full integer basis comparisons and the exact contractions in dimensions six and seven. The [higher-index framed-slide companion](higher-index-framed-slides-and-chain-maps.md#higher-slide-matrices) now realizes every elementary integral change with its full framed cobordism map and proves both neighbouring differentials using the singular-prism correction. The [receiving-dimension Whitney companion](whitney-moves-in-the-receiving-dimensions.md#receiving-whitney-flow) proves the full disk, adapted frame and supported move for the three required sheet-dimension pairs, with all original metric, orientation and framing maps retained. The [actual Morse realization and middle-cancellation companion](realizing-framed-handles-and-middle-cancellation.md#middle-six-seven-reduction) constructs the compatible function, proves the exact intersection-to-trajectory comparison and every escape and support hypothesis, and completes the simply connected smooth cobordism reductions in dimensions six and seven.",

          "number": 2,
          "complete_expected_argument_paragraph": "For completeness, the required second Chern pairings do not assume\nthat $R^+$ is K\\\"ahler. Applying Riemann--Roch to $A$ yields $c_2(R^+)A=0$,\nbecause $A^3$, $c_1(R^+)A^2$, and $c_1(R^+)^2A$ all vanish.",

        },

          "number": 3,
          "complete_expected_argument_paragraph": "The real tangent bundle of $W_A$ restricted to the normalization is\nthe sum of its real tangent bundle and this normal line. Here $[C]$ denotes its degree-four\ncohomology class on $R$. Since $H^2=-mH$, we have\n$(2H+m)^2=m^2=-2[\\mathrm{pt}]$. The surface $S$ has\n$p_1(S)=-24[\\mathrm{pt}]$. The ruled-bundle tangent sequence thus\ngives\n\\[\n p_1(R)+N_0^2=p_1(S)+2(2H+m)^2=-28[\\mathrm{pt}],\n\\]\nand $C\\cdot(a+hH)=aF$. This proves the covector formula.",

          "number": 1,
          "complete_expected_argument_paragraph": "\\begin{proof}\nWe first remove the bounded period units by a marked smooth\ndeformation.         },

          "number": 2,
          "complete_expected_argument_paragraph": "The fixed toric charts, with this extra parameter, therefore\ngive a smooth family of the same Mumford cusp quotients.\nThere is no new stabilizer at the central fibre: a nonzero\nperiod translates every height-one ray by a nonzero lattice\nvector, and cannot preserve any finite cone of the fan.\nThe usual finite fundamental collection of toric charts gives\nproper discontinuity, uniformly for the compact parameter\ninterval. Near the fixed spheres,\nchoose family equivariant normal tubular coordinates. After\nconjugating the negative-weight line the normal representation\nis scalar multiplication on $\\mathbb C^2$. Equivalently the Eells--Kuiper invariant changes\nsign. Applying this to the inverse loop proves the assertion.\nThe antiholomorphic symmetry therefore supplies no order-two restriction.\n\\end{proof}",

        }

          "text": "\n\\subsection{Finiteness and convergence of the actual sphere tower}\n\\label{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:adams-actual-convergence}\n\n\\label{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:section-11}\\label{courseIII:adams-tower:11}\n\nWe make explicit two ordinary-homology comparisons used at this step. For a connective CW spectrum \\(X\\), the filtration by its cells gives\n\n\\begin{equation}\n\\pi_a(H\\wedge X)=H_a(X;k).\n \\label{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:11.1}\n\\end{equation}\n\nIndeed the relative term for an oriented \\(j\\)-cell is \\(\\pi_a(\\Sigma^j H)\\), which by \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:9.7} is \\(k\\) when \\(a=j\\) and zero otherwise. On an infinite complex, each representative sphere and each nullhomotopy has compact image in a finite cell stage; filtered unions therefore commute with these groups. The identification is natural on cellular maps, and cellular approximation extends it to all maps.\n\nThe same cellular calculation identifies the right side of \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:11.1} with the level-space colimit used in \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:10.6}. The pair exact sequence, the prism identity and finite support show that this construction preserves cofibre sequences and increasing cell unions. On a sphere cell it gives \\(k\\) in its cell degree with the same positive generator. This proves the comparison, including the actual unit and all attaching maps. A connective spectrum can be given a connective CW replacement by adding spheres representing the missing homotopy classes, then cells killing the kernels, successively in each nonnegative degree. The relative disk extension argument is the stable version of the included CW construction; compactness of each representing sphere verifies the increasing-union step.           "line": 524,
          "text": "\n\\subsection{Realization, the actual fibre bundles and the suspension maps}\n\\label{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:adams-original-spectrum}\n\n\\label{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:section-9}\\label{courseIII:adams-tower:9}\n\nWe provide the topological comparison for \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:8.4}. For a simplicial set \\(V\\), its realization is the quotient of the disjoint union of \\(V_q\\times\\Delta^q\\), by the face and degeneracy identifications. A degeneracy collapses the corresponding adjacent barycentric coordinates by adding them. Repeatedly removing a degeneracy terminates, since the dimension decreases. The resulting nondegenerate simplex is unique: apply face right inverses to two proposed degeneracy expressions and move faces past degeneracies by the simplicial identities. If either expression had a remaining degeneracy, the proposed nondegenerate simplex would be degenerate; otherwise each simplex is a face of the other and they are equal. The same argument with the ordered lists of repeated indices shows that the two collapse maps agree. Hence the interiors of the nondegenerate simplices are disjoint cells, with their indicated characteristic maps. Their boundaries lie in the previous skeleton, and the quotient topology is exactly the weak topology for these characteristic maps. This proves the CW description. For \\(L_n=|K^n|\\), \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:8.6} gives finitely many cells in each dimension; when \\(n\\geq1\\) there is one vertex and no nondegenerate cell of dimension between zero and \\(n-1\\).\n\nHuman-source context for this realization is Greg Friedman, \\href{https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.4221v8}{arXiv:0809.4221v8}, original TeX 756--898. Its later discussion explicitly refers elsewhere for the general comparison between simplicial and topological homotopy. The following proof uses the actual abelian-group quotient bundles in \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:8.4}, and supplies their local sections and lifting maps here. It does not import that general comparison as an unwritten prerequisite.\n\nWe use two concrete facts about this realization. First it preserves finite products, with the compactly generated product topology. To construct the inverse to the evident product map, represent two points by their barycentric coordinates, take the union of the two lists of cumulative partial sums in \\([0,1]\\), and use the lengths of the resulting common subdivision as the new barycentric coordinates. Repeat each simplex vertex across the subintervals into which its old interval was divided. These are exactly degeneracy maps, so the resulting pair is a simplex of the product and maps to the original two points. The construction is independent of a further common subdivision. On each region specifying the order of the partial sums it is affine in the coordinates; the formulas agree on its boundary. Thus it is continuous on each product of characteristic simplices, and therefore in the compactly generated topology. This proves both inverse maps, including points with zero barycentric coordinates. Addition and inverse in a simplicial abelian group consequently realize to continuous group operations.\n\nSecond, let\n\n\\begin{equation}\n0\\longrightarrow A\\longrightarrow V\\xrightarrow{q}Q\\longrightarrow0"

          "text": "\nConversely define \\(S(c\\otimes d)\\) by triangulating \\(\\Delta^p\\times\\Delta^q\\) along all lattice paths from \\((0,0)\\) to \\((p,q)\\). Give a path the sign of the permutation of its horizontal and vertical steps relative to all horizontal steps followed by all vertical steps. Compose its affine simplex with \\((c,d)\\). Internal faces from paths interchanging adjacent unlike steps cancel; boundary faces give precisely \\(\\partial c\\otimes d+(-1)^p c\\otimes\\partial d\\). For \\(A\\), deleting a nonjoining vertex gives the matching tensor boundary and joining-vertex terms telescope. Hence both maps are chain maps, preserving augmentation.\n\n\\begin{lemma}[product chain equivalence]\n\\label{mapsI:chain:lemma:4.1}\n\\leavevmode\\par\nThe two maps are inverse up to natural chain homotopies, preserving products of subspaces.\n\\end{lemma}\n\\Uses{the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; the explicit constructions and calculations in the proof}\n\n\n\\begin{proof}\nHere is an explicit inductive construction of the needed homotopies. Chains in a convex set have a contraction to any fixed vertex: cone each singular simplex to that vertex by linear interpolation. The cone boundary identity gives \\(\\partial K+K\\partial=1-i\\epsilon\\), where \\(\\epsilon\\) is augmentation and \\(i\\) inserts the vertex. Tensoring two such contractions gives a contraction of their tensor complex to \\(\\mathbb Z\\): the homotopy is \\(K\\otimes1+(i\\epsilon)\\otimes L\\), with the tensor sign \\((-1)^{\\deg c}\\) in the second term. The first identity and then the second verify this formula; its boundary sum is \\(1-(i\\epsilon)\\otimes(j\\epsilon)\\).\n\nFor \\(1-SA\\), assume a homotopy \\(h\\) is already defined on lower-dimensional simplices. On the universal diagonal simplex \\(\\Delta^m\\to\\Delta^m\\times\\Delta^m\\), form\n\\(z=(1-SA)\\sigma-h\\partial\\sigma\\)."

          "text": "\n\\subsection{The finite cocycles and the full cochain spaces}\n\\label{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:adams-original-cocycles}\n\n\\label{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:section-8}\\label{courseIII:adams-tower:8}\n\nWe construct the coefficient object needed by the original tower. For every order-preserving map \\(\\theta:[r]\\to[q]\\), define the pullback by evaluating on the complete tuple \\((\\theta(i_0),\\ldots,\\theta(i_n))\\), including this zero rule.           "line": 524,
          "text": "\n\\subsection{Realization, the actual fibre bundles and the suspension maps}\n\\label{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:adams-original-spectrum}\n\n\\label{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:section-9}\\label{courseIII:adams-tower:9}\n\nWe provide the topological comparison for \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:8.4}. For a simplicial set \\(V\\), its realization is the quotient of the disjoint union of \\(V_q\\times\\Delta^q\\), by the face and degeneracy identifications. A degeneracy collapses the corresponding adjacent barycentric coordinates by adding them. Repeatedly removing a degeneracy terminates, since the dimension decreases. The resulting nondegenerate simplex is unique: apply face right inverses to two proposed degeneracy expressions and move faces past degeneracies by the simplicial identities. If either expression had a remaining degeneracy, the proposed nondegenerate simplex would be degenerate; otherwise each simplex is a face of the other and they are equal. The same argument with the ordered lists of repeated indices shows that the two collapse maps agree. Hence the interiors of the nondegenerate simplices are disjoint cells, with their indicated characteristic maps. Their boundaries lie in the previous skeleton, and the quotient topology is exactly the weak topology for these characteristic maps. This proves the CW description. For \\(L_n=|K^n|\\), \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:8.6} gives finitely many cells in each dimension; when \\(n\\geq1\\) there is one vertex and no nondegenerate cell of dimension between zero and \\(n-1\\).\n\nHuman-source context for this realization is Greg Friedman, \\href{https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.4221v8}{arXiv:0809.4221v8}, original TeX 756--898. Its later discussion explicitly refers elsewhere for the general comparison between simplicial and topological homotopy. The following proof uses the actual abelian-group quotient bundles in \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:8.4}, and supplies their local sections and lifting maps here. It does not import that general comparison as an unwritten prerequisite.\n\nWe use two concrete facts about this realization. First it preserves finite products, with the compactly generated product topology. To construct the inverse to the evident product map, represent two points by their barycentric coordinates, take the union of the two lists of cumulative partial sums in \\([0,1]\\), and use the lengths of the resulting common subdivision as the new barycentric coordinates. Repeat each simplex vertex across the subintervals into which its old interval was divided. These are exactly degeneracy maps, so the resulting pair is a simplex of the product and maps to the original two points. The construction is independent of a further common subdivision. On each region specifying the order of the partial sums it is affine in the coordinates; the formulas agree on its boundary. Thus it is continuous on each product of characteristic simplices, and therefore in the compactly generated topology. This proves both inverse maps, including points with zero barycentric coordinates. Addition and inverse in a simplicial abelian group consequently realize to continuous group operations.\n\nSecond, let\n\n\\begin{equation}\n0\\longrightarrow A\\longrightarrow V\\xrightarrow{q}Q\\longrightarrow0"

          "text": "\n\\subsection{Application to the original coefficient spaces and every suspension}\n\\label{courseIII:the-actual-mod-two-cooperation-comparison-through-degree-eight:actual-eight-original-suspension}\n\n\\label{courseIII:the-actual-mod-two-cooperation-comparison-through-degree-eight:section-4}\\label{courseIII:actual-degree8:4}\n\nLet \\(L_q=|K^q|\\) be the original simplicial-cocycle spaces of the Adams-tower companion.           "text": "\n\\subsection{Finiteness and convergence of the actual sphere tower}\n\\label{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:adams-actual-convergence}\n\n\\label{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:section-11}\\label{courseIII:adams-tower:11}\n\nWe make explicit two ordinary-homology comparisons used at this step. On an infinite complex, each representative sphere and each nullhomotopy has compact image in a finite cell stage; filtered unions therefore commute with these groups. The identification is natural on cellular maps, and cellular approximation extends it to all maps.\n\nThe same cellular calculation identifies the right side of \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:11.1} with the level-space colimit used in \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:10.6}. The pair exact sequence, the prism identity and finite support show that this construction preserves cofibre sequences and increasing cell unions. On a sphere cell it gives \\(k\\) in its cell degree with the same positive generator. Its cell filtration consequently has exactly the same original cellular differential as \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:11.1}, and a single surviving quotient in each total degree. This proves the comparison, including the actual unit and all attaching maps. A connective spectrum can be given a connective CW replacement by adding spheres representing the missing homotopy classes, then cells killing the kernels, successively in each nonnegative degree. The relative disk extension argument is the stable version of the included CW construction; compactness of each representing sphere verifies the increasing-union step.           "text": "\n\\subsection{Realization, the actual fibre bundles and the suspension maps}\n\\label{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:adams-original-spectrum}\n\n\\label{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:section-9}\\label{courseIII:adams-tower:9}\n\nWe provide the topological comparison for \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:8.4}. For a simplicial set \\(V\\), its realization is the quotient of the disjoint union of \\(V_q\\times\\Delta^q\\), by the face and degeneracy identifications. A degeneracy collapses the corresponding adjacent barycentric coordinates by adding them. Repeatedly removing a degeneracy terminates, since the dimension decreases. The resulting nondegenerate simplex is unique: apply face right inverses to two proposed degeneracy expressions and move faces past degeneracies by the simplicial identities. If either expression had a remaining degeneracy, the proposed nondegenerate simplex would be degenerate; otherwise each simplex is a face of the other and they are equal. The same argument with the ordered lists of repeated indices shows that the two collapse maps agree. Hence the interiors of the nondegenerate simplices are disjoint cells, with their indicated characteristic maps. Their boundaries lie in the previous skeleton, and the quotient topology is exactly the weak topology for these characteristic maps. This proves the CW description. For \\(L_n=|K^n|\\), \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:8.6} gives finitely many cells in each dimension; when \\(n\\geq1\\) there is one vertex and no nondegenerate cell of dimension between zero and \\(n-1\\).\n\nHuman-source context for this realization is Greg Friedman, \\href{https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.4221v8}{arXiv:0809.4221v8}, original TeX 756--898. Its later discussion explicitly refers elsewhere for the general comparison between simplicial and topological homotopy. The following proof uses the actual abelian-group quotient bundles in \\eqref{courseIII:the-adams-tower-and-exact-inverse-limits:eq:8.4}, and supplies their local sections and lifting maps here. It does not import that general comparison as an unwritten prerequisite.\n\nWe use two concrete facts about this realization. First it preserves finite products, with the compactly generated product topology. To construct the inverse to the evident product map, represent two points by their barycentric coordinates, take the union of the two lists of cumulative partial sums in \\([0,1]\\), and use the lengths of the resulting common subdivision as the new barycentric coordinates. Repeat each simplex vertex across the subintervals into which its old interval was divided. These are exactly degeneracy maps, so the resulting pair is a simplex of the product and maps to the original two points. The construction is independent of a further common subdivision. On each region specifying the order of the partial sums it is affine in the coordinates; the formulas agree on its boundary. Thus it is continuous on each product of characteristic simplices, and therefore in the compactly generated topology. This proves both inverse maps, including points with zero barycentric coordinates. Addition and inverse in a simplicial abelian group consequently realize to continuous group operations.\n\nSecond, let\n\n\\begin{equation}\n0\\longrightarrow A\\longrightarrow V\\xrightarrow{q}Q\\longrightarrow0"

        "courseIII:thom-euler-for-lesson11:CG-S6-CHAIN-THEOREM-5.2": {
          "file": "editorial/III_course/thom-euler-for-lesson11.tex",
          "line": 19,
          "text": "For an abelian group \\(M\\), choose a free presentation \\(0\\to J\\to F\\to M\\to0\\) and define\n\\(\\operatorname{Ext}(M,G)=\\operatorname{coker}(\\operatorname{Hom}(F,G)\\to\\operatorname{Hom}(J,G))\\).\nThis group does not depend on the presentation. Indeed a map between the quotient groups lifts to a map of the free groups by choosing preimages of their basis elements, and carries kernels to kernels. Two lifts differ by a map into the target kernel; precomposition by that difference becomes a restriction from the target free group and hence vanishes in the cokernel. Lifts of identity maps between two presentations therefore induce inverse cokernel maps. This also proves functoriality.\n\n\\label{courseIII:thom-euler-for-lesson11:CG-S6-CHAIN-THEOREM-5.2}\n\n\\begin{theorem}[universal coefficient exact sequence]\nFor a free abelian chain complex \\(K\\) there is a natural exact sequence\n\n\n\n```{=latex}\n\\[\n0\\to\\operatorname{Ext}(H_{m-1}(K),G)\n\\to H^m(\\operatorname{Hom}(K,G))\n\\to\\operatorname{Hom}(H_m(K),G)\\to0."

          "line": 30893,
          "text": "\nConversely define \\(S(c\\otimes d)\\) by triangulating \\(\\Delta^p\\times\\Delta^q\\) along all lattice paths from \\((0,0)\\) to \\((p,q)\\). Give a path the sign of the permutation of its horizontal and vertical steps relative to all horizontal steps followed by all vertical steps. Compose its affine simplex with \\((c,d)\\). Internal faces from paths interchanging adjacent unlike steps cancel; boundary faces give precisely \\(\\partial c\\otimes d+(-1)^p c\\otimes\\partial d\\). For \\(A\\), deleting a nonjoining vertex gives the matching tensor boundary and joining-vertex terms telescope. Hence both maps are chain maps, preserving augmentation.\n\n\\begin{lemma}[product chain equivalence]\n\\label{mapsI:chain:lemma:4.1}\n\\leavevmode\\par\nThe two maps are inverse up to natural chain homotopies, preserving products of subspaces.\n\\end{lemma}\n\\Uses{the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; the explicit constructions and calculations in the proof}\n\n\n\\begin{proof}\nHere is an explicit inductive construction of the needed homotopies. Chains in a convex set have a contraction to any fixed vertex: cone each singular simplex to that vertex by linear interpolation. The cone boundary identity gives \\(\\partial K+K\\partial=1-i\\epsilon\\), where \\(\\epsilon\\) is augmentation and \\(i\\) inserts the vertex. Tensoring two such contractions gives a contraction of their tensor complex to \\(\\mathbb Z\\): the homotopy is \\(K\\otimes1+(i\\epsilon)\\otimes L\\), with the tensor sign \\((-1)^{\\deg c}\\) in the second term. The first identity and then the second verify this formula; its boundary sum is \\(1-(i\\epsilon)\\otimes(j\\epsilon)\\).\n\nFor \\(1-SA\\), assume a homotopy \\(h\\) is already defined on lower-dimensional simplices. On the universal diagonal simplex \\(\\Delta^m\\to\\Delta^m\\times\\Delta^m\\), form\n\\(z=(1-SA)\\sigma-h\\partial\\sigma\\)."

          "text": "\nThe first row uses the suspension of the augmentation ideal, so its chain map has degree zero. Sections 2--7 prove all displayed maps; \\cref{courseIII:the-actual-mod-two-cooperation-comparison-through-degree-eight:section-8} proves the receiving permanent-cycle statement.\n\n\\subsection{The receiving degree-six cobar comparison}\n\\label{courseIII:the-actual-mod-two-cooperation-comparison-through-degree-eight:actual-eight-receiving-cobar}\n\n\\label{courseIII:the-actual-mod-two-cooperation-comparison-through-degree-eight:section-8}\\label{courseIII:actual-degree8:8}\n\nAt fixed cobar length \\(s\\), the full degree-six cohomology calculation has the three adjacent terms of total degree \\(s+6\\), at lengths \\(s-1,s,s+1\\).           "text": "\nThere is no interchange of an infinite sum with a product in this proof: \\eqref{courseIII:the-original-adams-tower-and-arithmetic-completion:eq:4.6} is a finite sum for each fixed degree and fixed \\(m\\).\n\n\\subsection{The actual equivalence of the two completions}\n\\label{courseIII:the-original-adams-tower-and-arithmetic-completion:arithmetic-adams-equivalence}\n\n\\label{courseIII:the-original-adams-tower-and-arithmetic-completion:section-5}\\label{courseIII:adams-arithmetic:5}\n\nRetain the Adams target and its unit\n\n\\begin{equation}\nY_X=\\operatorname*{holim}_{s\\geq0}(C_s\\wedge X),\n\\qquad u_X:X\\longrightarrow Y_X.\n\\label{courseIII:the-original-adams-tower-and-arithmetic-completion:eq:5.1}\n\\end{equation}\n"

          "text": "\nThis proves the vanishing in the actual cooperation cobar.           "text": "\n\\subsection{Vanishing in the actual odd-prime cooperation cobar}\n\\label{courseIII:the-original-odd-prime-cooperations-and-degree-six-adams-calculation:odd-actual-cobar}\n\n\\label{courseIII:the-original-odd-prime-cooperations-and-degree-six-adams-calculation:section-5}\\label{courseIII:odd-coop:5}\n\nUse the \\cref{courseIII:the-actual-mod-two-adams-resolution-and-cooperation-maps:cooperation-original-factors} defined by the original coefficient spectrum and its ordered factors; \\cref{courseIII:the-original-odd-prime-cooperations-and-degree-six-adams-calculation:section-6} below supplies their graded comparison at every odd prime. They are valid over \\(k\\): the shuffle cross product has its integer Koszul sign, the coefficient multiplication is associative and graded-commutative, and insertion of the original unit gives the coproduct.           "text": "\\section{The six-dimensional bundle comparison and the stable framing}\\label{courseIII:spin-six-and-the-framing-comparison:section}\n\nThe following complete arguments are retained as re-derivations of their classical prerequisites. Source-specific calculations and their hypotheses are stated explicitly.\n\nWe prove the following receiving result for lesson 7: for every oriented smooth homotopy six-sphere \\(\\Sigma\\), the original rank-seven bundle \\(T\\Sigma\\oplus\\mathbf1_{\\mathbb R}\\) is trivial. We retain the extra real line. The original tangent bundle has Euler number two and is not trivial. A stable framing is also not a framed null-cobordism; producing the latter is a further step in smooth sphere recognition.\n\nThe proof uses the polynomial loop reduction already proved in \\cref{courseIII:almost-complex-structures-and-integrability:sphere-classification}, and supplies its injectivity argument for the compact bases actually needed here. We then construct the full map \\(SU(4)\\to SO(6)\\), compute its Euler class, and use the actual frame fibration \\(SO(6)\\to SO(7)\\to S^6\\). The human context is Françoise Michel and Claude Weber, \\href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.0704v1}{\\emph{Michel Kervaire work on knots in higher dimensions}, arXiv:1409.0704v1}, Sections 2--3. Those original-author TeX sections were read; their statements of stable parallelizability, surgery and stable groups are not used as substitutes for the receiving proofs below.\n\n\\subsection{A family index for the actual loops}\n\\label{courseIII:spin-six-and-the-framing-comparison:framing-family-index}\n\n\\label{courseIII:spin-six-and-the-framing-comparison:section-1}\\label{courseIII:spin6:1}"

          "text": "\n\\subsection{Realizing one complete index stage}\n\\label{courseIII:realizing-framed-handles-and-middle-cancellation:middle-realize-stage}\n\n\\label{courseIII:realizing-framed-handles-and-middle-cancellation:section-2}\\label{courseIII:middle-cancel:2}\n\nSuppose a preceding cobordism has an outgoing regular level \\(N=f^{-1}(a)\\), with its full parametrization and metric retained.           "text": "\nConversely define \\(S(c\\otimes d)\\) by triangulating \\(\\Delta^p\\times\\Delta^q\\) along all lattice paths from \\((0,0)\\) to \\((p,q)\\). Internal faces from paths interchanging adjacent unlike steps cancel; boundary faces give precisely \\(\\partial c\\otimes d+(-1)^p c\\otimes\\partial d\\). For \\(A\\), deleting a nonjoining vertex gives the matching tensor boundary and joining-vertex terms telescope. Hence both maps are chain maps, preserving augmentation.\n\n\\begin{lemma}[product chain equivalence]\n\\label{mapsI:chain:lemma:4.1}\n\\leavevmode\\par\nThe two maps are inverse up to natural chain homotopies, preserving products of subspaces.\n\\end{lemma}\n\\Uses{the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; the explicit constructions and calculations in the proof}\n\n\n\\begin{proof}\nHere is an explicit inductive construction of the needed homotopies. The cone boundary identity gives \\(\\partial K+K\\partial=1-i\\epsilon\\), where \\(\\epsilon\\) is augmentation and \\(i\\) inserts the vertex. Tensoring two such contractions gives a contraction of their tensor complex to \\(\\mathbb Z\\): the homotopy is \\(K\\otimes1+(i\\epsilon)\\otimes L\\), with the tensor sign \\((-1)^{\\deg c}\\) in the second term. The first identity and then the second verify this formula; its boundary sum is \\(1-(i\\epsilon)\\otimes(j\\epsilon)\\).\n\nFor \\(1-SA\\), assume a homotopy \\(h\\) is already defined on lower-dimensional simplices. On the universal diagonal simplex \\(\\Delta^m\\to\\Delta^m\\times\\Delta^m\\), form\n\\(z=(1-SA)\\sigma-h\\partial\\sigma\\)."

          "line": 294,
          "text": "\n\\subsection{The exact product map after cancellation}\n\\label{courseIII:morse-cancellation-with-controlled-support:morse-product-map}\n\n\\label{courseIII:morse-cancellation-with-controlled-support:section-6}\\label{courseIII:morse-cancel:6}\n\nSuppose \\((C;M_0,M_1)\\) is a compact smooth cobordism, and \\(f:C\\to[0,1]\\) equals the boundary collar coordinate near each boundary.
